annotations.text:
Phase 1 — one job only: "my playlists are broken".

They still exist, but their tracks will not load, because the files moved. Repair repoints the collection entries those playlists reference.

Rebuilding a DELETED playlist from a written tracklist is a separate job the tool already does (build-playlist) — it gets its own entry point later, never a branch of this one.

Every screen holds four constraints:
· preview always precedes a write
· an output that collides with an input disables writing
· fingerprinting may be unavailable, and says so
· the tag cache is the only file written before you confirm

Read left to right, top to bottom.

2b, 3b and 3c are branches off the main path, not extra steps: stopping a scan, the review table opened up, and the two review outcomes that ask a different question from "is this the right file?".

The Interaction spec page carries the keyboard map, the status and confidence tokens, and the accept/reject rules that these screens draw from.

3c is one screen only in this canvas — in the running wizard it is the same detail rail as 3b, filled with a refuted and a re-encoded candidate.

It is drawn separately because the two rails carry the whole argument: a refuted candidate must show WHAT contradicts and by how much, and a re-encode must show the evidence FOR it, since its tier is a weak one.

Neither adds a status colour.

This page is the contract the wizard screens are built against.

If a screen and this page disagree, this page is wrong — fix it here, then fix the screen.
